records.real_world_identity_notes: PMR's Vertigo resolves to the Gillet Vertigo Streiff 2004 race specification represented by the existing gillet-vertigo-streiff record. PMR uses N-GT as its game taxonomy; the documented 2004 Spa entry ran in the historical G2 class, while PMR's own history article describes the car as part of the N-GT FIA-GT context. The exact 2004/surviving-chassis evidence supports six-speed sequential hardware. It does not establish the driver's clutch, cut, blip, shift-interface, or original wheel procedure.
records.confidence_basis: PMR's official car page and its 2004-spec article identify the Gillet Vertigo and its 2004 specification. OverTake's contemporary report identifies the game car as the 2004 Gillet Vertigo Streiff, and Racing Sports Cars records the exact chassis YA9VA2900Y0169021 at the 2004 Spa 24 Hours as a Gillet Vertigo Streiff. The same chassis is the surviving FIA-GT car described by RaceArt, whose current dossier specifies a Tractive six-speed sequential gearbox. These sources bridge the abbreviated PMR telemetry name to the existing curated record without treating the simulator controls as real-car evidence.

Both exact-chassis and PMR sources identify the transmission as sequential. Manual blip is a downshift action in this controls model; no upshift-blip claim is asserted. Automatic blip is a downshift action in this controls model; no upshift-blip claim is asserted. Throttle lift is represented as an upshift action in this controls model; no separate downshift-lift claim is asserted.
